key_insight: Preserving recovered execution procedures in refined artifacts raises mean ML reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6% while reducing downstream API spending by 19.7%.
engineering_relevance: Packaging code, environments, launchers, and reproduction guidance can make research handoffs more reliable and less dependent on the coding agent used.
method: Use ReproBridge agents to preserve recovered procedures and decisions in standardized reproducible artifacts.
Package a refined codebase, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide.
Compare fresh-session reproduction using raw code versus refined artifacts, with a separate Auditor checking execution evidence.
evidence_signal: ReproBridge-Bench contains 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 papers, with five human-verified reference scores per task; all four evaluated models exceed 90% mean success with refined artifacts.
watch_item: The reported downstream API savings do not establish net savings after the cost of constructing refined artifacts.
paper_title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
